Revised assessment incorporating the Financial Stability Report (FSR): The FOMC statement is credibly accommodative and pro-growth—keeping rates at the ELB until inflation moderately exceeds 2% and continuing sizable Treasury and agency MBS purchases anchors expectations and eases credit conditions, supporting demand. However, the FSR (May 2021) flags vulnerabilities that temper the outlook: elevated risk appetite and stretched asset valuations (reflected in a compressed equity risk premium as of March 2021), sensitivity of asset prices to rate increases amid low interest rates, lingering stress in commercial real estate linked to CMBS, earlier‑2021 mortgage delinquencies/forbearance overhang, and fragilities in nonbank intermediation and short‑term funding markets observed during the pandemic. Against these, the FSR also underscores strong bank capital and ongoing monitoring of financial vulnerabilities. Net effect: still moderately positive given policy support and anchored expectations, but more cautious than a growth‑only read.
